explanations.8: The $host and $request_uri are nginx variables that represent the domain name and the full path with query string, so this line keeps users on the same URL they requested but upgrades it to HTTPS.
explanations.13: This tells nginx to listen on port 443 (the secure HTTPS port) and support both SSL encryption and the HTTP/2 protocol for faster connections.
explanations.28: TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3 are the modern secure protocols for HTTPS; older versions are intentionally excluded for security reasons.
explanations.30: This is a list of encryption algorithms nginx can use; the weird syntax means 'use the strong ones but exclude the broken ones like MD5 and NULL encryption'.
explanations.43: This line makes nginx try to serve the requested file, then try a folder, and if neither exists, fall back to index.html so client-side routing in Docusaurus works.
explanations.47: The ~* pattern matches file extensions for common static files (images, fonts, etc.), and the $ means 'only if the URL ends with these extensions'.
explanations.50: After setting a long cache time, try_files =404 ensures nginx returns a 404 error if the static file doesn't actually exist instead of falling back to index.html.
